messages:
maria: Quick q — thinking about tenant-scoped permission profiles that also control routing policies + quota attribution. Do we have a design for a single UI + API that surfaces and enforces boundaries? Example: tenant A allowed model-x, blocked model-y, and a per-route quota cap.
ash: We don't have a single surface today. UX concern: exposing routing knobs to tenant admins could be risky. Maybe surface an 'allowed models' list and keep routing policy decisions in platform-managed presets.
kevin: +1 to allowed-models list. For the API, propose an entitlements endpoint: 
```json
POST /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/entitlements
{
  "version": "2026-03-01",
  "allowed_models": ["llama-3-70b-q4", "redwood-embedded-v1"],
  "route_overrides": [{"route": "/generate", "quota": 100000}],
  "policy_mode": "enforce" /* preview | enforce */
}
```
That lets us support preview vs enforced modes.
samir: Small API debate: should entitlements be additive (merge with org defaults) or full-override? Additive is safer for platform defaults, overrides are simpler for audits. Also token propagation question: do we evaluate entitlements based on tenant token on request path or via service account with tenant header?
iris: Telemetry: we need audit trails for every change + an event that increments when a request is rejected due to policy. Metric ideas: `policy.rejections.count` and `policy.effective_version` per request span. Also include policy version in traces to debug post-rollouts.
oliver: Rollout UX idea: offer a 'preview' change where you show a diff and simulated effects for 24h before enforcement. Console should show affected routes + estimated blocked request count from last 30 days.
maria: :thumbsup: Diff preview is great. Also thinking about where quota lives — entitlements vs route config. If quota sits in entitlements we get central visibility, but tying quota to routes makes usage easier to reason about in console.
ash: Edge case: large enterprise customers with nested sub-tenants — we need inheritance and an explicit UI indicator for "inherited vs local" permissions and a warning when editing inherited rules.
kevin: Implementation note: routing decisions need to be O(1) on the request path. Suggest we compile entitlements into a signed, versioned blob that's cached on each serving node. Blob payload = tenant_id + policy_version + allowed_model_set. Signed to prevent tampering.
samir: Security note: the signed blob must be invalidatable for emergency revokes. Need a fast invalidation path (global publish of a revocation list or bump a revocation counter in config).
iris: Telemetry follow-up: store `policy_version` as a tag on every request span. That will let us correlate error spikes with policy changes quickly.
oliver: I'll mock a console panel: "Effective Entitlements" + a "Simulate change" checkbox that shows which routes would be blocked and quota impacts. Will post a Figma.
access-bot: access-bot: Created epic INF-4321 "tenant entitlements + routing" and added maria, ash, kevin, samir, iris. Link: https://go/repo/INF-4321
maria: Next steps: kevin to prototype API contract, oliver to mock UI, iris to define telemetry events and tags, samir to design revocation path. Sync tomorrow 10am? @kevin @oliver @iris @samir
kevin: I'll post an API sketch before EOD today.
ash: I'll draft UX concerns and add a short list of admin guardrails to the epic.
maria: Awesome — thanks all.
